comment:
Loved this video and I can agree with many of your choices as I have stayed long term at many!
I spent a month in Medellin and the weather is perfect and the same all year round!  I spent 3 
Months in Costa Rica in 2010 and it was good.  I did rent a car often but mostly on 3 day weekends to go outside the village I was living to go around the country.  Roads aren’t great but rentals were cheap and they delivered car to my condo whenever I needed it!  
I stayed a month in Valencia in 2021.  It was awesome.  Very walkable and beach wasn’t too far away!
I have been to Croatia 3 times.  Up north for a long weekend, in 2023 for a week and in 2022 for a month.  The month and the week were in Split.  Love Split.   I got to Dubrovnik and a few of the islands during month.  Travel by ferry’s everywhere.  So easy! I need to go to Zagreb!  

I am going to Krakow in a couple weeks for a couple weeks!  

I would recommend Buenos Aires for a long term stay. I have been 3x.  Once in 2016 for 3 months, in 2018 for 2 months and then in 2024 for 1 month.  Good expat community and it is very European feeling!

My favorite trip was 2012 for 3 months was to Cap d’Ail, France (borders Monaco). My home base (best airbnb ever) was overlooking the Sea….i could literally throw a stone into ocean. comment:
Great video. as a person who has done slow travel in southern Thailand for a year I can tell you there is so much to experience and so many different vibes to experience  in different areas

Hua hin is the Expat Haven, but I disliked  it. It felt like living in the suburbs in the US.
 The Andaman sea  side of thailand is my favorite because it offers so much more. Krabi, phi phi island, railey beach are all spectacular
Koh lanta is more rustic, and original thai vibe. Koh yai noi is even more rural and I could not wait to leave
Phuket is now my  homebase 
Being such a large island, it has so many different beach areas and each one has a different feel
I thought I hated Phuket until I found the right area that fits me perfectly

@@UnknownHumanOnline Malta is a lovely island in the Mediterranean Sea and has no doubt about that. Malta is known for its history, beautiful views, and warm weather. However, some travelers might find it challenging for a few reasons.
As per our view it mainly because of the summer heat which can be very intense, often reaching over 30°C. This can make outdoor activities uncomfortable. Secondly, the beaches are mostly rocky, which might not be what you expect if you want sandy shores.
Getting around can also be tricky. Driving in Malta can be chaotic, and parking is often difficult to find. Public buses are available but may not be very reliable.
To make your trip better, we suggest you to consider visiting in spring or fall when the weather is cooler. Drink plenty of water and wear sunscreen to protect yourself from the sun. If you can, rent a car for easier travel, but be careful on the roads.

Like everywhere else, the affordability of Portugal, especially housing, is rapidly decreasing. And it is not immigration, as some suggest. It is hedge funds and high net worth individuals buying up the housing and raising prices.

Basically you need to go to a country adjacent to Belarus, Ukraine, or Russia to still find reasonable rates. Or basically places that are very cold or very hot.

Great video. as a person who has done slow travel in southern Thailand for a year I can tell you there is so much to experience and so many different vibes to experience  in different areas
Gulf Coast side, Koh Samui, koh tao and koh panang are all enjoyable and different.  I love the laid back hippie vibe of koh tao and the diving snd snorkeling. On koh samui  you will find different vibes, depending on which part of the island you are on. 
Hua hin is the Expat Haven, but I disliked  it. It felt like living in the suburbs in the US.
 The Andaman sea  side of thailand is my favorite because it offers so much more. Krabi, phi phi island, railey beach are all spectacular
Koh lanta is more rustic, and original thai vibe. Koh yai noi is even more rural and I could not wait to leave
Phuket is now my  homebase 
Being such a large island, it has so many different beach areas and each one has a different feel
I thought I hated Phuket until I found the right area that fits me perfectly 
So whenever you decide to do southern Thailand, I would suggest that it will take you more than three months. Maybe three months on the gulf side and three or four months on the andamen sea side
I just spent rainy season in Phuket and found it delightful. They were very few days when it rained so much I could not go out. The prices were lower. The crowds were less, and the hotels were cheaper. Temperature was also cooler.

#Visit #SriLanka #2024

One of the best travel destination. We have two seasons. 

November to April the Winter Season and Best Season to travel to a tropical paradise like Sri Lanka. 

White Sand Beaches and Sky blue water. 
Wildlife Safari and The most beautiful train ride in Asia through hill countries. 

The Eastern Part is a hidden gem where many tourists don't travel to. Arugam Bay is known as one of the best surfing beaches in the World. 

Kalpitiy in Puttalam is known for Kite-Surfing. 

Here from hot climate to temperate climate can be felt within hours of travel time. 

The world's highest leopards density in a wildlife park from Yala National Park and the world's highest density of waterfalls. 

35C°-8C° wide range of temperature rage. 

Tea Plantations are the highlight. 

If you visit Anuradhapura, you will witness how rich the history is here. You can see 2500 years old ancient ruins and Dagobs. And the World's Oldest Human-Planted Tree in the World. 
2500 Years old which is a branch of the original Bodhi tree of where the Lord Buddha attained the Enlightenment.

author: @hmbabaali1179
comment: A list that doesn't include Uganda is incomplete. Sir Winston Churchill called it the Pearl of Africa for a reason! The people,  floral and fauna are second to none. You want wild life, you got it. The rush green of the country will make you wanna stare for ages. You want to go to the northern hemisphere,  start from Uganda.  If you change your mind in 2 seconds,  you cross over to the southern hemisphere. If you're undecided as where to go, you can stand in both hemispheres at once. I'm talking about the Equator! You want white sand beaches,  go to Lake Victoria or Ssese Islands. You want to see the source of  the longest river in the world,  Jinja is waiting for you, you want water rafting on river Nile, Itanda falls are yours to discover. You want some cold temperature, head to Mt Rwenzori in the west. It has the most snow and ice in all of Africa. You have never seen primates, it all starts in Uganda. You wanna go fishing, Lake Victoria and other numerous lakes are waiting for  you. Expect Tilapia or the gigantic Nile Perch. You want falls, head to Murchison Falls and see how the mighty River Nile is forced thru a narrow gorge with thundering noise. Don't forget to look out for the Nile Crocodiles.  I assure you, you will never get lost in the mighty and vast Imaramagambo and Mabira forest, but you will be treated to a scene of numerous and a variety of birds. Are you interested in volcanic activities,  head to the west of the country and check out Kitagata. No need to buy coffee or tea. Just scoop water from the geyser in a cup and mix with your Arabic or Robust coffee or tea. While at it, you can boil your eggs by simply dipping them in water. From there you can head to the game parks to see the big 5 and a lot more. Uganda's game parks are the wettest in Africa with the rain distributed throughout the year. Therefore all fauna have dark colours compared to the game in other countries.  This phenomenal is magnified more so in birds. In Uganda, you can experience all the 4 geographical seasons in one country on the same day!! I could go on until eternity and still not do justice to the beauty of Uganda. reply_text:
@@GeorgiosStarakis   Chalkidiki is a very beautiful place where most of the north greek citizens  prefer to spend their summer holidays .

Thassos is also a georgeous island on the northern part of Greece , which is combining unique beaches ( like Porto Vathy , a one-of-a-kind beach with tropical like sea and marble around it ) and a mountain , with some traditional places , taverns monuments , stores , topical museums etc

Kerkyra is also a very astonishing place , that despite being an island , it has some city-like parts , not with the polution , the big crowds or other cons of an actual city . There you can find a dozen of interestingly activities and little art shops . It has a lot of places to visit too like a castle , a samurai museum etc (I heard that you can even play cricket there ) . If you are a family man then you should really consider taking your family there .

A quite interesting destination to go would be Agio Oros ( or Athos ) . Its the third "leg" of Chalkidiki . It's a total different experience from any other destination . It's a holy place for christians and there for there are a lot of monasteries where you can stay . You can go there whether your a christian or not . The place has something really magical about it . The floras are magnificent  and some of them are really extraordinary . The life there is very peaceful . There you can find inner peace , have a better understanding of god , communicate eeeeasily with the other visiters and in general it's a great trip for your spirit . Every time you leave from there you feel like a different person , cleansed and free . Although I must say that you  should think carefully about going there , due to the rules that you must follow , like not being able to listen into music , eating only at specific times , not going out after a specific time , waking up really early , I mean it's even illegal for women to go there ( there is a backstory for this ) . But it's a magical trip non-the-less.

Another great destination would be Skopelos , a family friendly island place at the center of the North Kyklades . From there you can visit the neighboring islands like Allonisos , Skiathos or Skyros , since they are pretty close one to another.

The most beautiful island at the Aegean must be Crete . What's not to like about Crete? They have amazing beaches , traditional food , liquor , herbs , landmarks , monuments , even castles and the citizens are so unique friendly that there is no way that you could not love them .

Of course , if you would prefer not to go to an island you should definitely try to visit Nauplio , and try to lose your self in it's narrow and filled with life streets , walk near to its beautiful sea and of course visit it's monuments .

But , if you want to visit a lot of archaeological sites than you should consider taking a tour of Peloponnesos , and of course try to visit Hydra , an island where (nearly) no cars exist , it's fortress and the museum , and Spetses . But bear in mind that in those islands you can learn more about the greek revolution (1821) and not about the ancient civilizations.

author: @nicoguerrero3854
comment: Albania?! Are you high?
reply_text: Yes, Albania! If you stop watching TV and Hollywood movies and actually go out to see the world, you'll see for yourself! I have been to almost every country in Europe and nowhere else I have seen such crystal clear water and wild, virginal beaches. The friendliest people I met were also in Albania, I got invited for free drinks to a bar with the locals! The food, nature and towns are indescribable! Not too mention the guesthouses with the amazing views over the Ionian Sea for 10 eur per person! Now let's compare Albania to the most overrated destination - Thailand. I have been to Thailand recently and it was the most disappointing country ever. Yes, if you haven't bee anywhere else (or only to those over touristy places) you might love Thailand. However, I haven't been to a country where I would meet so many rude people, where I would be scammed and given wrong information everywhere, even in official tour agencies. At one point I was even threatened with murder and this was the worst experience of my life. The beaches in Thailand are difficult to enjoy with all those western tourists (surprisingly no locals having fun on the beaches - locals do only selling and scamming the 'rich' white tourists). I dislike this division. During the full moon party, the sea is literally turning into urine! Not too mention that even the famous edible insects are just for show for tourists and you have to pay to take a photo of them. It simply lacks authenticity. I like the pure, real, raw places that are not just four mass tourism (Albania, Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, Turkmenistan, Bosnia, Peru, Iceland and many others) and this is why I made this list. I always got the same responses as yours from my friends when I said I'm going to Albania. Later, when I showed them the photos, suddenly everybody wants to go there! Please, people don't listen to mainstream media! Go and see the world for yourself!
